resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com lists an L-4 tower for the 1930s. The 1933 Choteau paper calls the summit structure a glass lookout, and the December 1933 notice calls it a lookout house. The story reports both; the record uses L-4 tower because it is the only type named by firelookout.com.
Firelookout.com gives 8,855 feet; the October 1933 Choteau paper gives 8,865 feet above sea level. The story gives both.

Firelookout.com dates a camp to the 1920s, and a 1931 newspaper item mentions guards at the Mt. Wright lookout before the 1933 construction. The sources do not say what stood on the summit before 1933.

notes_for_editor: Dates and staffing come from newspaper items quoted secondhand on the Montana lookouts page; the originals (Choteau Acantha, Independent Record, Billings Gazette) were not checked. The 1933 foreman is spelled Knutzon, Kundtzon and Knudtzon in different items; the story avoids naming him. Design and elevation conflict as recorded. The hiking guide describes a radio tower and small building at the summit but does not say whether either is the lookout; its photos date to March 2019 and its check-in to July 2022. The access note rests on that guide. The brief's access 'unknown' is updated to public on the basis of that guide, and the brief's gone status is confirmed by firelookout.com and the Montana list.
